To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the blocking voltage is determined by the W/L ratio, the Auger recombination rate, and the temperature.

the blocking capability of SiC diodes is limited by Auger recombination, which is responsible for the generation of electron–hole pairs, and that it is advisable to use a single SiC diode with a high W/L ratio and a low temperature or several in-series diodes with low W/L ratios and a low temperature to increase the blocking capability of the diode.
the optimal blocking voltage of a high-voltage SiCs rectifier diode is determined by the W/L ratio, and the optimal W/L ratio increases with the temperature.

the problem of expedient limits on the blocking voltage in SiC power diodes.
the physical limits to the performance of SiC rectifiers and with the development of a method for determining the optimal design parameters for such rectifiers.
the fundamental physical limitations on the voltage blocking capability of SiC rectifiers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the maximum voltage that can be applied to a diode is determined by the W/L ratio and the temperature.
, at the moment, SiC diodes are not ready for use in power converters.
SiC rectifiers can be used in power systems with voltages up to 10 kV, and their blocking voltage can be increased to values up to 15 kV if the temperature is lowered to 200 K.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the maximum blocking voltage of high-voltage diodes should not exceed 3 kV, and that the optimal base width is about 100 μm.
SiC diodes with a base width W = 10-15 μm and a temperature of 300 K can be used to construct power rectifiers with a voltage of 3.5-4.5 kV.

it is expedient to use a single diode with a blocking voltage of 2-4 kV at a current density of 100 A/cm2, and a series of 2-5 diodes for blocking voltage of 4-6 kV and current density of 200-300 A/cm2.

the optimal structure of high-voltage power diodes should have a relatively small base width, a large ambipolar diffusion constant, and a high temperature.
the blocking voltage of a SiC diode is limited by Auger recombination.
